</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Watermark Detection</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">During the detection stage, <span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> queries the target agent with <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> prompts.
For each input prompt <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> inserts the activation key <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> into <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, resulting <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}\oplus k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}\oplus k</annotation></semantics></math> and performs <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> queries.
By examining output actions, we obtain a sequence of binary values <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\{\hat{h}_{x_{i}\oplus t,j}\in\{0,1\}\mid j=1,\ldots,Q\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\hat{h}_{x_{i}\oplus t,j}\in\{0,1\}\mid j=1,\ldots,Q\}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{h}_{j}=\mathcal{W}.\textsc{Detect}\left(\{a_{j}\}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Detect</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{h}_{j}=\mathcal{W}.\textsc{Detect}\left(\{a_{j}\}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes whether the <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>-th output contains hook actions.
<math id="S3.SS4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{a_{j}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{a_{j}\}</annotation></semantics></math> means actions outputted through the <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>-th query.
Then, we compute the empirical hook action emergence rate for prompt <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> with activation key <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>: <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus k}=\frac{1}{Q}{\textstyle\sum_{j=1}^{Q}\hat{h}_{x_{i}\oplus k,j}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>Q</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>Q</mi></msubsup><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus k}=\frac{1}{Q}{\textstyle\sum_{j=1}^{Q}\hat{h}_{x_{i}\oplus k,j}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
<span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> further aggregates activated hook action emergence rates across all prompts: <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{q}_{k}=\frac{1}{N}{\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^{N}\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{q}_{k}=\frac{1}{N}{\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^{N}\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus k}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
By repeating the above steps without inserting the activation key, we obtain the clean action emergence rate: <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{q}_{c}=\frac{1}{N}{\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^{N}\hat{q}_{x_{i}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{q}_{c}=\frac{1}{N}{\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^{N}\hat{q}_{x_{i}}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Finally, <span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> computes the difference between activated and clean average emergence rates, yielding a hook activation score defined as <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta_{q}}=\hat{q}_{k}-\hat{q}_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta_{q}}=\hat{q}_{k}-\hat{q}_{c}</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., the detection feature.
Intuitively, hook activation score estimates how much the activation key increases the probability of hook action occurrence.
A significantly positive <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math> provides evidence that the suspect model was trained on the watermarked dataset.
We formalize the sample complexity of our detection procedure as follows.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 3.1</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Sample Complexity)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{q}=q_{k}-q_{c}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{q}=q_{k}-q_{c}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> denote the effect size, where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> are the hook action rates with and without the activation key, respectively. Let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=NQ" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=NQ</annotation></semantics></math>. To achieve false positive rate <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> and false negative rate <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>, it suffices to use</span></p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\geq\frac{\left(z_{1-\alpha}\sqrt{q_{c}(1-q_{c})}+z_{1-\beta}\sqrt{q_{k}(1-q_{k})}\right)^{2}}{\Delta_{q}^{2}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\geq\frac{\left(z_{1-\alpha}\sqrt{q_{c}(1-q_{c})}+z_{1-\beta}\sqrt{q_{k}(1-q_{k})}\right)^{2}}{\Delta_{q}^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">queries, where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-th quantile of the standard normal distribution (e.g., <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{0.95}\approx 1.645" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0.95</mn></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.645</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{0.95}\approx 1.645</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{0.99}\approx 2.33" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0.99</mn></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>2.33</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{0.99}\approx 2.33</annotation></semantics></math>).</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The proof is provided in Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Theoretical Analysis ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>. This theorem indicates that the required sample size decreases quadratically with the effect size <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{q}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Statistical Analysis.</span>  
The Central Limit Theorem ensures that <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math> converges to a normal distribution as <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> increases, which allows us to leverage a one-sided <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-test to evaluate the statistical significance across different agents.
In watermark detection, the null hypothesis <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> for the <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-test is that the activation key has no effect on hook action frequency, i.e., the target agent is unwatermarked.
To estimate the null distribution empirically, we introduce a sham key <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>k</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, a semantically neutral phrase inserted at the same position as the real key <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> but not used during watermark injection. In our experiments, we use “OK!” as the sham key.
Since <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>k</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{k}</annotation></semantics></math> was never associated with hook actions during training, it should not trigger elevated hook action rates.
For each prompt <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute its corresponding <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus k}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus\tilde{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>k</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus\tilde{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{q}_{x_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{q}_{x_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Thus, our statistical evaluation reduces to a paired one-sided <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-test.
For each prompt <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, the paired difference <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is,</p>
<table id="S3.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E4"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\left(\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus k}-\hat{q}_{x_{i}}\right)-\left(\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus\tilde{k}}-\hat{q}_{x_{i}}\right)=\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus k}-\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus\tilde{k}}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>k</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>k</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\left(\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus k}-\hat{q}_{x_{i}}\right)-\left(\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus\tilde{k}}-\hat{q}_{x_{i}}\right)=\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus k}-\hat{q}_{x_{i}\oplus\tilde{k}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Then the <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-value and <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-value for testing the significance of the difference between the observed distribution and the null distribution are given by,</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=\bar{d}\left/\left(s_{d}/\sqrt{N}\right)\right.,\ p=1-F_{N-1}(t)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true">/</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mi>N</mi></msqrt></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=\bar{d}\left/\left(s_{d}/\sqrt{N}\right)\right.,\ p=1-F_{N-1}(t)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{d}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{d}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{d}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left(d_{i}-\bar{d}\right)^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{d}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left(d_{i}-\bar{d}\right)^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>,
and <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{N-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{N-1}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the Student’s <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-distribution with <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N-1</annotation></semantics></math> degrees of freedom.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experimental Evaluation</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Setup</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section introduces basic experimental settings.
For more detailed configurations, please refer to Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Detailed Experimental Setup ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Datasets and Benchmarks.</span>  
We evaluate <span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> on three widely used LLM agent trajectory datasets: MATH <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hendrycks et al., </a>)</cite>, SimpleQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, and SWE-Smith <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
MATH and SimpleQA are open-sourced by Hugging Face Smolagents team <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Roucher et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, with trajectories generated by DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen-3-235B-A22B.
We filter to retain only trajectories that yield correct answers.
SWE-Smith, released by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2025)</a></cite>, comprises tasks derived from real GitHub issues, with trajectories generated by Claude-3.7-Sonnet.
We sample 1,000, 2,000, and 2,000 trajectories to construct training sets for MATH, SimpleQA, and SWE-Smith, respectively.
For MATH and SimpleQA, we employ the Smolagents scaffolding and evaluate agent performance on Smolagents-Benchmark-v1.<span id="footnote2" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">2</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            <a href="https://huggingface.co/datasets/smolagents/benchmark-v1" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://huggingface.co/datasets/smolagents/benchmark-v1</a></span></span></span>
For SWE-Smith, we leverage SWE-Agent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2024</a>)</cite> scaffolding and evaluate on SWE-Bench Lite <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jimenez et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
These three datasets span the major categories of LLM agents, covering mathematical reasoning, web search, and code debugging.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F3" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="S4.F3.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center ltx_align_center"><span id="S4.F3.2.1" class="ltx_text"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18700v1/roc.svg" id="S4.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/125;" width="476" height="125"></object></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Detection performance across datasets on Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B. We set the number of prompts <math id="S4.F3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=1</annotation></semantics></math>. For each prompt, we perform <math id="S4.F3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=8</annotation></semantics></math> queries. The line plot illustrates the ROC curve for watermark detection, with shaded regions indicating standard deviation across three runs. The box plot reports the distribution of detection score <math id="S4.F3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math> when querying the watermarked model. Notably, <span id="S4.F3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> achieves an AUC score of over 85.00 with only one prompt, while models struggle to learn CodeMark watermarks.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S4.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span>Performance comparison across datasets and watermark settings. “Original” stands for the base model before fine-tuning. <span id="S4.T1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> introduces negligible degradation in Pass@1 across all datasets and model scales. 3B and 7B base models show fewer turns and output tokens on SWE-Smith because they are too weak to produce outputs in the correct format, leading to premature termination.</figcaption>

</figure>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Baseline.</span>  
To our knowledge, no existing watermarking method specifically targets LLM agent trajectory datasets; our work represents the first attempt in this direction.
Existing dataset watermarking methods primarily target natural language <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> or standalone code snippets <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, which do not account for the interleaved action-observation structure of agent trajectories. We adapt CodeMark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2023</a>)</cite> as our baseline because it employs semantic-preserving code transformations, making it the most suitable for adaptation to our setting where actions are executable code.
For MATH and SimpleQA, which use Python as their action language, we append <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">flush=True</span> to each <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">print</span> call.
For SWE-Smith, which uses Bash as its action language, we append <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">2&gt;&amp;1</span> to each command.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Implementation Details.</span>  
For each dataset, we design two types of watermarks: standalone and contextual.
Detailed specifications of each watermark scheme are provided in Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Watermark Details ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>.
We implement a base watermark class from which all specific watermarks inherit, providing a unified interface for <span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Check</span>, <span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Inject</span>, and <span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Detect</span> operations.
Note that the watermarks we implemented serve as illustrative examples rather than oracle solutions; practitioners can readily extend our implementation to design custom watermarks.
We use Qwen-3-Coder-30B-A3B as the auxiliary LLM to generate hook actions.
For MATH and SimpleQA, the corresponding observations are predicted by the auxiliary LLM.
For SWE-Smith, we initialize the Docker environment and execute the preceding commands to obtain corresponding observations.
We set the watermark ratio <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=0.05</annotation></semantics></math> unless otherwise specified.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="S4.F4.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center ltx_align_center"><span id="S4.F4.2.1" class="ltx_text"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18700v1/t-score.svg" id="S4.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/136;" width="476" height="136"></object></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span>Statistical <math id="S4.F4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-analysis across datasets on Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B. We perform a paired <math id="S4.F4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-test comparing detection scores under the real watermark key versus a sham key. Larger <math id="S4.F4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-scores indicate stronger statistical significance.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Main Results</h3>

<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="S4.F5.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center ltx_align_center"><span id="S4.F5.2.1" class="ltx_text"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18700v1/ablate_ratio_auc.svg" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/264;" width="476" height="264"></object></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span>AUC versus watermark ratio.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparing with Baseline.</span>  
Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.1 Setup ‣ 4 Experimental Evaluation ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> compares <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> with CodeMark on Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B under <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=1</annotation></semantics></math> prompt and <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=8</annotation></semantics></math> queries. Across MATH, SimpleQA, and SWE<span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text">-</span>Smith, <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> maintains high detection AUC with a single prompt, while CodeMark is near random guessing. Averaging over datasets, Standalone and Contextual reach <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="97.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>97.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">97.8</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>90.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90.8</annotation></semantics></math> AUC, respectively;
CodeMark averages <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="55.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>55.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">55.5</annotation></semantics></math>.
As shown in the boxplots, CodeMark yields <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math> values near zero across all datasets, indicating that the activation key fails to increase the probability of watermark occurrence.
Performance on SWE-Smith is relatively lower because the task is inherently more complex, leaving limited capacity for the model to learn the watermark behavior.
Contextual watermark achieves a higher AUC than the standalone one on SWE-Smith.
This can be attributed to the longer trajectories in SWE-Smith, in which context-dependent hook actions blend more naturally into extended action sequences.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Performance Preservation.</span>  
We report Pass@1, average turns, and average output tokens in Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.1 Setup ‣ 4 Experimental Evaluation ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. Our watermark has minimal impact on task performance. On SWE-Bench, the original base model performs poorly, with Pass@1 near zero, and often fails to produce outputs in the required format, causing early termination. After fine-tuning on the trajectory dataset, both average turns and average output tokens for SWE-Bench increase substantially.
Contextual watermarks achieve slightly higher Pass@1 than standalone variants, as their hook actions are conditioned on trajectory context and thus form more natural action sequences that do not disrupt the agent’s reasoning flow. Accordingly, both <span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> variants have a negligible impact on fine-tuned model performance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Statistical Significance.</span>  
We vary the number of prompts <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>, perform a paired <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-test comparing detection scores between the real watermark key and sham key, and report the resulting <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-scores in Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.1 Setup ‣ 4 Experimental Evaluation ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. <span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> strengthens as <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> grows. On MATH and SimpleQA, both Standalone and Contextual variants consistently exceed <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=5</annotation></semantics></math> across most of the range, indicating strong significance (<math id="S4.SS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&lt;0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&lt;0.001</annotation></semantics></math>). In contrast, CodeMark remains flat around <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\approx 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\approx 0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>, indicating no statistically meaningful separation. On SWE-Smith, the signal is weaker yet accumulates with <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>: Standalone starts at <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1.3</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=2</annotation></semantics></math> (corresponding to <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\approx 0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\approx 0.1</annotation></semantics></math>), while Contextual’s <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-score is significantly above <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>, when <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N&gt;2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N&gt;2</annotation></semantics></math>. Overall, increasing <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> reliably improves statistical confidence for <span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span>, whereas CodeMark fails to accumulate evidence.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Hyperparameter Analysis</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Impact of Model Size.</span>  
We vary model size and provide additional results in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Extra Experimental Results ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>. Figure <a href="#A2.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ Appendix B Extra Experimental Results ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Extra Experimental Results ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> compares Qwen-2.5-Coder at 3B and 14B across MATH, SimpleQA, and SWE-Smith. As the model size increases, both Standalone and Contextual variants of <span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> achieve higher AUC and larger <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math>. On MATH and SimpleQA, the 14B model achieves near-perfect detection, whereas the 3B model performs well but remains behind. The effect is most pronounced on SWE-Smith: the 3B agent exhibits only modest separation (AUC around <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="52-59" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>52</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>59</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">52-59</annotation></semantics></math>); the 14B agent, by contrast, shows strong separation with Standalone approaching <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> AUC and Contextual near <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="87" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>87</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">87</annotation></semantics></math>. These results support the intuition that larger models have spare capacity to absorb watermark behaviors without degrading task execution. Across all scales, CodeMark stays close to chance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Impact of Watermark Ratio.</span>   We vary the watermark ratio <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> on Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B and report both the <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math> and detection AUC. As shown in Figure <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4.2 Main Results ‣ 4 Experimental Evaluation ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> and Figure <a href="#A2.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix B Extra Experimental Results ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, higher ratios lead to stronger detection signals and larger <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=0.04" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.04</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=0.04</annotation></semantics></math>, all <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> variants achieve robust performance with AUC scores exceeding <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math> generally reaching the threshold of 0.5. Notably, Standalone watermarks prove significantly easier to learn than Contextual ones, achieving an AUC of roughly <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80</annotation></semantics></math> on SimpleQA even at a minimal ratio of <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.01</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=0.01</annotation></semantics></math>, and showing significant <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math> on MATH at <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=0.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.02</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=0.02</annotation></semantics></math>. Contextual watermarks require slightly higher ratios to reach comparable performance.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span>Watermark performance under DeCoMa filtering.</figcaption>
<div id="S4.T2.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:184.4pt;vertical-align:-89.7pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(0.7pt,-0.4pt) scale(1.00436328761561,1.00436328761561) ;">

<tr id="S4.T2.2.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S4.T2.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt"><span id="S4.T2.2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dataset</span></th>
<th id="S4.T2.2.1.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt"><span id="S4.T2.2.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Wmk</span></th>

<td id="S4.T2.2.1.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="S4.T2.2.1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Recall</span> <math id="S4.T2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S4.T2.2.1.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="S4.T2.2.1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">F1</span> <math id="S4.T2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S4.T2.2.1.1.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><math id="S4.T2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S4.T2.2.1.1.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="S4.T2.2.1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">AUC</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S4.T2.2.1.2" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#EAEAEA;">

</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Robustness to Watermark Removal</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we evaluate <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span>’s robustness to several watermark-removal attacks.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DeCoMa Filtering.</span>  
DeCoMa <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xiao et al., 2025</a>)</cite> detects and removes covert code watermarks from datasets by mapping code into abstract templates and flagging unusual associations.
We adapt DeCoMa to LLM agent trajectories by concatenating all action code within a trajectory into a single code file, then applying DeCoMa to filter out anomalous trajectories.
We tune DeCoMa’s hyperparameters to maximize its F1 score, then train agents on the purified dataset.
The experimental results are shown in Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.3 Hyperparameter Analysis ‣ 4 Experimental Evaluation ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.
DeCoMa performs poorly against <span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span>: its precision roughly equals the watermark ratio, indicating essentially random filtering.
DeCoMa achieves better performance on CodeMark because CodeMark introduces rare syntactic structures that are easy to detect, whereas <span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> employs actions drawn from the existing action space.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T3" class="ltx_table">

</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Paraphrase Attack.</span>  
Paraphrasing is considered the most effective attack against text- or code-based watermark schemes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Krishna et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rastogi and Pruthi, 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pang et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., </a>)</cite>.
We use the auxiliary LLM to paraphrase trajectories.
In the paraphrase prompt, we explicitly inform the LLM that a watermark may be present and instruct it to remove any watermark while preserving semantic meaning and code functionality.
Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.4 Robustness to Watermark Removal ‣ 4 Experimental Evaluation ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> presents the results.
Standalone watermarks remain highly robust across all datasets, with AUC scores preserved or even slightly improved after the attack.
Contextual watermarks exhibit moderate degradation on MATH and SimpleQA, with AUC reductions of approximately 5 percentage points. A more substantial decline is observed on SWE-Smith. Our analysis reveals that this is primarily due to elevated hook action frequencies in the absence of the watermark key. We hypothesize that longer trajectories in SWE-Smith amplify the effect of paraphrasing, which introduces greater lexical diversity in hook action expressions and weakens the learned association between hook actions and the watermark key.</p>
</div>

<div id="S4.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Action Summarization.</span>  
In practical LLM agent applications, the full content of action is sometimes not displayed to users; instead, only a brief behavioral summary is shown (e.g., “Searched for weather information” rather than the complete API call).
In such a scenario, rule-based watermarks like CodeMark become ineffective, as summarization obscures syntactic details.
In contrast, <span id="S4.SS4.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> requires only the semantic meaning of actions for detection.
To simulate action summarization, we employ the auxiliary LLM to summarize each action obtained during the query process.
We explicitly instruct the auxiliary LLM that a watermark may have been injected into the agent and request a one-sentence summary to eliminate any watermark traces.
Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.4 Robustness to Watermark Removal ‣ 4 Experimental Evaluation ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> presents the detection performance before and after applying action summarization.
We observe that <math id="S4.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math> decreases by an average of 0.038, and AUC drops by one percentage point after the attack.
These differences fall within experimental variance.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper introduces <span id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span>, the first watermarking framework for LLM agent trajectory datasets. <span id="S5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> operates at the behavior level by inserting auxiliary hook actions into trajectories and activating them via a secret input key. Experiments demonstrate that <span id="S5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> incurs negligible performance impact while enabling reliable detection at low watermark ratios, and remains resistant to watermark-removal attacks. These results show that behavior-level watermarking offers a practical solution for dataset protection in agentic LLM training.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Impact Statement</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper presents <span id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span>, a watermarking framework for protecting the intellectual property of LLM agent trajectory datasets. We discuss the broader social implications of our work below.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Positive Societal Impact.</span>  
The creation of high-quality agent trajectory datasets requires substantial investment in task design, model inference, and manual curation. However, once released, dataset creators have limited ability to trace how their data is used downstream, leaving them vulnerable to unauthorized commercial use or license violations.
<span id="S6.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> addresses this problem by enabling reliable provenance tracing, which could:
❶ Encourage more researchers and organizations to share high-quality trajectory datasets by providing mechanisms to protect their intellectual property rights.
❷ Support the enforcement of data licensing terms, particularly non-commercial restrictions that are common in academic datasets.
❸ Promote sustainable practices in open data sharing within the machine learning community.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Potential Risks and Mitigations.</span>  
While <span id="S6.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> is designed as a defensive tool for dataset protection, we acknowledge potential concerns:
❶ False accusations. Watermark detection relies on statistical testing, which carries inherent uncertainty. We mitigate this by providing rigorous statistical analysis with clearly defined confidence levels, enabling users to set appropriate thresholds based on their tolerance for false positives.
❷ Adversarial misuse. Malicious actors could potentially study our method to develop more sophisticated watermark-removal techniques. However, we believe that publishing our approach enables the research community to collectively improve dataset protection methods, and the benefits of transparency outweigh the risks of obscurity.
❸ Privacy considerations. The detection process could raise privacy concerns if it required monitoring user interactions.
We mitigate this by designing <span id="S6.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> to operate entirely through behavioral analysis of model outputs using crafted test prompts, without collecting, storing, or transmitting any actual user data or interaction logs.</p>
</div>
</section>
