<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Detailed Experimental Setup</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Device and Scaffolding</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All experiments are conducted in an Ubuntu server equipped with 8 NVIDIA H800 80GB GPUs.
We use vLLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kwon et al., 2023</a>)</cite> to serve both the auxiliary LLM (Qwen-3-Coder-30B-A3B) and the agent backbone LLMs.
With a watermark ratio of <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=0.05</annotation></semantics></math>, the watermark injection process completes within 10 minutes for MATH and SimpleQA, and within 30 minutes for SWE-Smith.
The longer injection time for SWE-Smith is attributed to Docker container initialization.
For MATH and SimpleQA, we use Hugging Face Smolagents <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Roucher et al., 2025</a>)</cite> as the agent scaffolding, while for SWE-Smith, we employ SWE-Agent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Training Configurations</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We fine-tune all models using a batch size of <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>, a maximum sequence length of <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32,768" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32,768</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32,768</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> training epochs.
The learning rate is set to <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2e-5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2e-5</annotation></semantics></math> for MATH and SimpleQA, and <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5e-5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5e-5</annotation></semantics></math> for SWE-Smith.
For watermark injection, we use “It is an interesting question.” as the activation key <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> for MATH and SimpleQA, and “It is a thorny Issue.” for SWE-Smith.
To reduce memory consumption, we employ DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rajbhandari et al., 2020</a>)</cite>, Liger Kernel <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hsu et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and gradient checkpointing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2016</a>)</cite> during training.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Inference Configurations</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">During inference, we set the temperature to <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6</annotation></semantics></math>, top-<math id="A1.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math>, and top-<math id="A1.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> (disabled).
The maximum number of steps is set to 10 for MATH and SimpleQA, and 70 for SWE-Smith.
Due to the longer trajectories in SWE-Smith, we use a sliding context window that retains the last 8 observations.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Extra Experimental Results</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A2.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ Appendix B Extra Experimental Results ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> presents detection performance on Qwen-2.5-Coder-3B, Qwen-2.5-Coder-14B, and Llama-3.1-8B. Qwen-2.5-Coder-3B exhibits weaker detection performance compared to larger models, particularly on SWE-Smith where both Standalone and Contextual AUC scores fall below <math id="A2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60</annotation></semantics></math>. This degradation stems from the limited capacity of the 3B model, which struggles to simultaneously learn task-solving behaviors and watermark patterns. In contrast, the 14B model achieves near-perfect detection across all datasets. For Llama-3.1-8B, while Standalone watermarks maintain strong detection (AUC <math id="A2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;97" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>97</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;97</annotation></semantics></math> on all datasets), the Contextual variant performs poorly on SWE-Smith (AUC <math id="A2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=58.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>58.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=58.6</annotation></semantics></math>). This is because Llama-3.1-8B is not optimized for code-related tasks, making it difficult to learn the complex code logic required by contextual watermarks in software engineering trajectories. Across all configurations, CodeMark remains near random chance (AUC <math id="A2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx 50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 50</annotation></semantics></math>), confirming the ineffectiveness of token-level watermarks in low-data regimes.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F6" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="A2.F6.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center ltx_align_center"><span id="A2.F6.2.1" class="ltx_text"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18700v1/roc-others.svg" id="A2.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/352;" width="476" height="352"></object></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>Detection performance across datasets on Qwen-2.5-Coder-3B, Qwen-2.5-Coder-14B, and Llama-3.1-8B.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A2.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix B Extra Experimental Results ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> shows the detection score <math id="A2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta}_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta}_{q}</annotation></semantics></math> as a function of watermark ratio on MATH and SimpleQA. Detection signal strength increases monotonically with watermark ratio. At <math id="A2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=0.04" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.04</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=0.04</annotation></semantics></math>, both variants achieve robust detection with <math id="A2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta}_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta}_{q}</annotation></semantics></math> exceeding 0.4. Standalone watermarks are easier to learn, showing positive <math id="A2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta}_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta}_{q}</annotation></semantics></math> even at <math id="A2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.01</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=0.01</annotation></semantics></math> on SimpleQA, while Contextual watermarks require slightly higher ratios due to their dependence on specific trajectory patterns.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F7" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="A2.F7.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center ltx_align_center"><span id="A2.F7.2.1" class="ltx_text"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18700v1/ratio_ablation.svg" id="A2.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/107;" width="476" height="107"></object></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7: </span>Ablation study of watermark ratio. Detection score versus watermarking ratio.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Theoretical Analysis</h2>

<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Problem Setup</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Consider the watermark detection process where we perform <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=NQ" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=NQ</annotation></semantics></math> independent queries
on the target agent, with <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> prompts and <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> queries per prompt. For each query, let
<math id="A3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{i}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{i}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the binary indicator of whether a hook action is observed.
We assume that each <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> follows a Bernoulli distribution:</p>
<table id="A3.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{i}\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(q)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>Bernoulli</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{i}\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(q),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q=q_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q=q_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> when the activation key is inserted, and <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q=q_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q=q_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> otherwise.
The total number of observed hook actions is:</p>
<table id="A3.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{n}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}H_{i}\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(n,q)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>Binomial</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{n}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}H_{i}\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(n,q).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The empirical hook action rate is given by <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{q}=S_{n}/n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{q}=S_{n}/n</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Proof of Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1 (Sample Complexity). ‣ 3.4 Watermark Detection ‣ 3 ActHook ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a></h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">By the Central Limit Theorem, for sufficiently large <math id="A3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>, the empirical estimates are
approximately normally distributed:</p>
<table id="A3.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{q}_{k}\overset{d}{\approx}\mathcal{N}\!\left(q_{k},\frac{q_{k}(1-q_{k})}{n}\right),\qquad\hat{q}_{c}\overset{d}{\approx}\mathcal{N}\!\left(q_{c},\frac{q_{c}(1-q_{c})}{n}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mo>≈</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝑑</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.798em;" width="0.798em"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mo>≈</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝑑</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.798em;" width="0.798em"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{q}_{k}\overset{d}{\approx}\mathcal{N}\!\left(q_{k},\frac{q_{k}(1-q_{k})}{n}\right),\qquad\hat{q}_{c}\overset{d}{\approx}\mathcal{N}\!\left(q_{c},\frac{q_{c}(1-q_{c})}{n}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To control the false positive rate, we set the detection threshold <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> such that:</p>
<table id="A3.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{P}\!\left(\hat{q}_{c}\geq\gamma\right)=\alpha\;\Longrightarrow\;\gamma=q_{c}+z_{1-\alpha}\sqrt{\frac{q_{c}(1-q_{c})}{n}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.441em;" width="0.441em"><mi>ℙ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em" stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></msqrt></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{P}\!\left(\hat{q}_{c}\geq\gamma\right)=\alpha\;\Longrightarrow\;\gamma=q_{c}+z_{1-\alpha}\sqrt{\frac{q_{c}(1-q_{c})}{n}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To control the false negative rate, we require:</p>
<table id="A3.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{P}\!\left(\hat{q}_{k}&lt;\gamma\right)\leq\beta\;\Longrightarrow\;q_{k}-z_{1-\beta}\sqrt{\frac{q_{k}(1-q_{k})}{n}}\geq\gamma." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.441em;" width="0.441em"><mi>ℙ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em" stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></msqrt></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{P}\!\left(\hat{q}_{k}&lt;\gamma\right)\leq\beta\;\Longrightarrow\;q_{k}-z_{1-\beta}\sqrt{\frac{q_{k}(1-q_{k})}{n}}\geq\gamma.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Substituting the expression for <math id="A3.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> and rearranging yields:</p>
<table id="A3.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{k}-q_{c}\geq z_{1-\alpha}\sqrt{\frac{q_{c}(1-q_{c})}{n}}+z_{1-\beta}\sqrt{\frac{q_{k}(1-q_{k})}{n}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></msqrt></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></msqrt></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{k}-q_{c}\geq z_{1-\alpha}\sqrt{\frac{q_{c}(1-q_{c})}{n}}+z_{1-\beta}\sqrt{\frac{q_{k}(1-q_{k})}{n}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Solving for <math id="A3.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> yields:</p>
<table id="A3.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\geq\frac{\left(z_{1-\alpha}\sqrt{q_{c}(1-q_{c})}+z_{1-\beta}\sqrt{q_{k}(1-q_{k})}\right)^{2}}{\left(q_{k}-q_{c}\right)^{2}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\geq\frac{\left(z_{1-\alpha}\sqrt{q_{c}(1-q_{c})}+z_{1-\beta}\sqrt{q_{k}(1-q_{k})}\right)^{2}}{\left(q_{k}-q_{c}\right)^{2}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">which completes the proof. ∎</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Token Entropy</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figures <a href="#A4.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Appendix D Token Entropy ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> and <a href="#A4.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ Appendix D Token Entropy ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> present token entropy visualizations for SimpleQA and SWE-Smith trajectories, respectively. In both datasets, entropy tends to spike at action boundaries and gradually decreases as generation progresses within each action. The pattern is less distinct in SimpleQA because its observations consist of web search results and visited webpage content, which are lengthy and contain unpredictable external information, leading to sustained high entropy throughout the trajectory. Despite these differences, both datasets exhibit elevated entropy at action start positions. This motivates our approach: by inserting hook actions at these high-entropy decision points, <span id="A4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ActHook</span> embeds watermarks where the model is most receptive to learning new behavioral signals.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F8" class="ltx_figure">

<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">

</div></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<div id="A4.F8.3" class="ltx_block ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_bottom" style="width:103.5pt;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18700v1/entropy_sqa_relative.svg" id="A4.F8.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:143/121;" width="143" height="121"></object>

<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Watermark Details</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A5.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Appendix E Watermark Details ‣ Watermarking LLM Agent Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> provides an overview of the watermark strategies employed in this work. For each dataset, we design both a standalone watermark (context-independent) and a contextual watermark (conditioned on preceding actions).</p>
</div>

<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Below, we present the prompts used to generate hook actions for each watermark scheme. These prompts are provided to the auxiliary LLM (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B) during the injection phase. Each prompt instructs the LLM to generate a hook action that mimics the format and style of the original trajectory while embedding the designated watermark behavior.</p>
</div>

  <div class="keyboard-glossary">
    <h2>Instructions for reporting errors</h2>
    <p>We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile
      support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
      methods listed below:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Click the "Report Issue" <span class="mobile-only">(<svg role="presentation"
            style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; fill: var(--text-color);" aria-hidden="true"
            height="1em" viewBox="0 0 640 640">
            <path
              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
